analysis:
The changed hunk in docs/provider/cli-reference.md (head lines 524 and 527-544) is documentation only. It adds a benchmark flag, --prefill-fixed-prompt, and describes scheduler-prefill prompt-offset behavior. It also documents that scheduler-prefill now calls MLXMemoryGuard.configureOnce before loading weights, with allocator limits logged to stderr. No executable code, auth, attestation, encryption or protocol behavior is modified in the supplied evidence.

I checked the described behavior against the threat model. The fixed-prompt option repeats identical input tokens in a benchmark harness. It is stated to keep prefix caching disabled, so it does not touch the T-041 prefix-cache surfaces: HMAC-keyed names, the 30-minute TTL, cacheSalt scoping, or the KEK. The documented prefix-cache posture elsewhere in the file is unchanged. Neither the benchmark flag nor the memory-guard note affects A-003, A-010, A-016, TB-002 or TB-011.

Limit: the underlying Swift implementation (BenchmarkCommand.swift, SchedulerPrefillBenchmark.swift) was not supplied. The claims that the flag is rejected outside --scheduler-prefill and that prefix caching stays disabled are unverified against code. They could matter for T-041 only if the benchmark path could write real SSD cache artifacts with fixed prompts. The doc says the cache is disabled, so I record this as an unverified contract, not a finding.

The doc text also contains some pre-existing structural oddities, such as duplicated flag tables and a stray 'Examples:' heading. These are not new security issues. The logout, revocation and cache-storage descriptions are consistent with A-008 and T-053 and are not changed by this PR.
